entertainment.body:
Logo text Melanie Lysnkey’s next TV series will keep her at Paramount+ .

The Yellowjackets star will lead and executive produce a limited series currently titled Mushroom Murders at the streamer. Created by Anya Beyersdorf ( Apple Cider Vinegar ), Daina Reid ( The Handmaid’s Tale ) and Deb Balderstone ( Dustfall ) and produced by Soapbox Pictures, the drama is based on a notorious 2023 homicide case in Australia.

Here’s the description: “In 2023, Erin Patterson (Lynskey) served individual beef wellingtons to her estranged in-laws and their relatives at a lunch in her Victoria home in Australia. Unbeknownst to her guests, Patterson allegedly prepared the food with highly toxic death cap mushrooms, resulting in the deaths of three guests. The limited series depicts the 97 days between the now infamous lunch and Patterson’s subsequent arrest.” Related Stories TV Bill Murray Is Generally OK Giving You a "Bill Murray Moment" Business Paramount+ Head of Originals Jane Wiseman Exits as Skydance Streaming Unveils New Structure

“This is an ambitious series that brings a gripping real-life story, that captivated Australia and the world, to the screen with the scale, quality and creative vision audiences expect from Paramount+,” said Beverley McGarvey, president of Network 10 and head of streaming for Paramount Australia. “It is a powerful addition to our growing slate of premium storytelling, and we are delighted to partner with such an exceptional creative team to share it with viewers around the world. We are also thrilled to welcome Melanie Lynskey , whose remarkable talent will be integral to the series both on screen and as an executive producer.”

Lynskey will next be seen in the final season of Yellowjackets , which premieres Nov. 20 on Paramount+. Her recent work also includes the Netflix movie Don’t Say Good Luck , a guest role on CBS’ Matlock (opposite her husband, Jason Ritter) and season one of The Last of Us , which involved a different kind of mushroom murder. She is repped by Gersh.

Beyersdorf, Reid (who will direct all six episodes), Balderstone and Lynskey will executive produce the series with Xavier Marchand and Paramount+’s Sophia Mogford. Beyersdorf, Dianne Taylor and Belinda Chayko are writing the series.

entertainment.title: Watch NE-YO Perform National Anthem at Game 4 of 2026 World Series in Tampa Bay
entertainment.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are looking to complete the sweep to capture the franchise's first championship.
entertainment.body:
NE-YO performed the national anthem at game 4 of the 2026 World Series on Tuesday night (Oct. 27) in Tampa Bay, as the Milwaukee Brewers have their brooms out looking to complete the sweep of the Rays.

Holding his hat at his side, NE-YO brought his silky-smooth vocals to “The Star-Spangled Banner,” singing on the baseball field as a graphic of the American flag waved behind him. Watch the full performance here:

The R&B singer followed in the footsteps of Mickey Guyton (game 1), Kylie Cantrall (game 2) and Carly Pearce (game 3) as the national anthem performers in this year’s Fall Classic.

“You go over the words like a madman,” NE-YO said in an interview with MLB Network prior to the performance. “Lord knows that you don’t want to get up there and forget the words. You do a lot of vocal exercises… I try to keep it somewhat traditional.”

If the Rays snatch a victory, game 5 will take place on Wednesday (Oct. 28) at the Trop. But it could be a historic night at Tropicana Field. The champagne bottles are sure to be popping if the Brewers indeed win game 4 to capture the franchise’s first World Series championship.

2026 marks the Brew Crew’s first appearance in the Fall Classic since 1982, when they fell short to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games, which was when the franchise was still in the American League.

This is far from NE-YO’s first time singing the national anthem at a major sporting event. The “So Sick” artist previously performed at the 2016 NBA All-Star Game, Thanksgiving’s Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears game in 2021 and the inaugural NBA In-Season Tournament’s final in 2023 in Las Vegas between the Indiana Pacers and Los Angeles Lakers.

Sporting a cowboy hat, the 47-year-old returned in July with the release of his country-inspired Highway 79 album.

entertainment.title: Demi Lovato Offers Update After Allergic Reaction & Reported Hospitalization
entertainment.summary: The pop star blamed passion fruit or sushi for the medical emergency in a since-deleted post.
entertainment.body:
Demi Lovato is feeling “fine” after a reported brief hospitalization from an allergic reaction she had on Tuesday (Oct. 27).

According to People , the pop star posted a photo to her Instagram Story receiving medical treatment with an IV in her arm while wearing a hospital bracelet.

Lovato hypothesized that she developed a new allergy to either passionfruit or sushi. “Soooooo i’m either allergic to passionfruit or sushi now,” she wrote before deleting the post.

The 34-year-old reportedly made a follow-up post to quell the nerves of Lovatics around the globe as she’s recovering from the health scare. “I’m fine,” Lovato added in the also since-deleted post.

The “Sorry Not Sorry” has battled various allergies over the years. In 2009, she suffered an allergic reaction while filming an episode of Sonny With a Chance , which she believed was from an ingredient in an egg salad.

“I had to go home early because they couldn’t just cover me up with makeup since I was red and itchy,” Lovato said to Just Jared Jr. “I guess I was allergic to something in egg salad. But it was actually really funny and amusing.”

Lovato’s also been open about being badly allergic to pets like cats and dogs, but that didn’t stop the singer from adopting a feline, which she returned after one day.

On the music front, the Camp Rock alum released her dance-pop album It’s Not That Deep in October 2025, which peaked at No. 9 on the Billboard 200.

entertainment.title: JoJo Talks 20 Years of ‘The High Road,’ Collaborating With Tommy Hilfiger & First F1 Race: ‘I Like to Drive Fast, Bi—!’

entertainment.body:

JoJo may not have been in the driver’s seat for her first F1 race last weekend in Austin, but she could have been.

“I like to drive fast, bi—! I love to go fast,” she told Billboard backstage at Proper Presents: Soundtracks with Tommy Hilfiger , a music series held at Austin Proper Hotel in collaboration with the iconic American fashion house ahead of the race. “I love to whip a car around,” JoJo says. “I want to be in that car.”

Despite having never attended an F1 race prior to Circuit of the Americas (COTA), the singer says she’s done her research, noting that Tommy Hilfiger is the official apparel sponsor for the Cadillac Formula 1 Team, which is making its debut season on the grid. Growing up, JoJo fell in love with Cadillac by way of a friend’s family ride, calling it “the fanciest car in town. It was just so cool,” she says. “The fact that Tommy is [working] with Cadillac makes me feel so nostalgic.” Related 'The Voice': Four-Chair Turn Cade Mower Moves on After Battle Round LISA Drops New Limited-Edition Merch for Her PlayStation Collab: Shop the BLACKPINK Star's Designs Online Here Are the 33 Best Christmas Gifts for Gamers to Shop Online in 2026 Explore JoJo See latest videos, charts and news

That nostalgia extends to the clothing brand itself. “My introduction to Tommy was when Aaliyah was rocking Tommy ,” JoJo says, shouting out the late singer and 90s fashion star. “Being preppy but also streetwear is something that really resonates with me because I love to inhabit that space,” JoJo continues. “I appreciate the classic Americana cool of it. As somebody who moved to New York three years ago, I am always looking for that wearability and that cool. It’s no surprise that Tommy has [maintained] that cultural relevance.”

For his part, Hilfiger says that his brand’s integration into pop culture wasn’t an accident; it’s by design.

“I’ve always believed fashion is part of the conversation, but it’s only one part of culture. You have to be curious about what people are listening to, who they’re watching, and what they’re excited about. That’s where the energy comes from,” the designer shares. “For me, art, music, celebrity, and sport have always been connected to fashion. They’re all ways people express who they are and what they want to be part of.”
